title: Checked at compile time
description:
A `consteval` function **must** run during compilation. That makes it a validator: bad input is a compile error instead of a bug found later.

Write `consteval std::uint32_t rgb(std::string_view hex)`. It takes a colour written as `"#RRGGBB"` (upper or lower case hex digits) and returns it as the number `0xRRGGBB`.

If the text is not exactly `#` followed by six hex digits, **throw** something. A `throw` that is actually reached during constant evaluation is not allowed, so the compiler stops with an error that points at the offending call.

Write a small `constexpr` helper to convert one hex digit to its value.
hints: Start `value` at 0. For each digit: `value = value * 16 + digit`. That shifts what you have one hex place to the left and adds the new digit.
